steps.text: Pep Rally
The whole school in the gym. The band plays the fight song in a key that doesn't exist.

steps.speaker: kelly
steps.text: Smile. Everyone's watching the new kid. And everyone's watching me watch you.
The mascot costume sits on a folding chair by the bleachers. Empty. Nobody wanted to wear it this year. Nobody says why.
The squad needs one more for the human pyramid.
Club Fair
Folding tables line the hallway. Every club has a sign, a sign-up sheet and one person trying too hard.
You can join one or two. They'll take your After School on their days, every week. Choose like your afternoons matter. They do.
Test Week
The posters go up overnight: TEST WEEK. Somebody has drawn a skull on every one. The skulls are crying.
Your classes this week are exams. Your stats and your attendance decide the grades. The report card comes Friday.
Report Card
An envelope with your name on it, sealed with the school crest. It's heavier than paper should be.
The Dance
Paper stars on the gym ceiling. A disco ball that only half turns. Everyone you know, dressed like someone else.
The DJ plays the slow song. Then, under the music, something else plays. Water. Running water, from everywhere at once.
The lights flicker. Outside, the fountain in the town square has started to run. It hasn't run in thirty years.
The Fountain
The fountain doesn't run. It breaks. Water, then light, then the other town, pouring up out of the ground into the square.

steps.speaker: kelly
steps.text: That's not the woods. That's HERE.

steps.speaker: theo
steps.text: Both towns. At once. That's not supposed to be possible.
For the first time, the narrator has nothing to say.
The Morning After
The fountain is a crater now, glowing faintly blue. The town put a ribbon around it. The ribbon is not helping.
Curfew posters on every door. The buses stop at six. Somebody spray-painted WE SAW IT on the town hall.

steps.speaker: innocent_bystander
steps.text: Huh. A portal. Neat. Anyway, the bakery's out of muffins.

then.text: Mr. B's office is empty. His name is gone from the door. Diane's post has eleven thousand shares.

else.text: Mr. B gives a statement on the local news: a gas main, he says. Nobody believes him. Nobody says so.

steps.text: And around town, small cracks of the other place have opened in daylight. Leak points. Something keeps climbing out.
Sunday night. The crater hums. The train station's lights come on for the first time in thirty years.
Up on the hill, a window in the abandoned mansion opens. Then closes. Then opens.
...Ahem. Sorry. Lost my place there for a moment. It won't happen again.
End of Act 1
